uncited: Method-Specific Training Configurations define the hyperparameters, optimization loops, and architectural adjustments required to train specific Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) variants.
This family of methods solves the problem of translating theoretical NeRF formulations into stable, convergent training procedures for diverse datasets and hardware constraints.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Training Loop Setup](1522-training-loop-setup.md) and [Learning Rate Scheduling](2701-learning-rate-scheduling.md) by providing the concrete numerical values, loss functions, and network structures unique to each variant (e.g., NeRF, Mip-NeRF, DONeRF), rather than generic procedural steps.
The children in this family share the fundamental goal of minimizing the photometric error between rendered images and ground truth inputs via gradient descent.
All methods utilize differentiable volume rendering to compute gradients with respect to the neural network parameters.

Common structural elements include the use of Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to map spatial coordinates and viewing directions to density and color, and the use of ray sampling strategies to query these networks.
However, the specific activation functions, sampling densities, loss formulations, and optimizer settings vary significantly to address artifacts like aliasing, dark pixels, or memory constraints.
A simplified training setup for the Blender dataset, designed for speed rather than maximum accuracy.
It uses one round of sampling, 128 samples for the proposal MLP, and 32 samples for the NeRF MLP.
The proposal MLP has 4 layers and 256 hidden units, while the NeRF MLP has 8 layers and 256 (or 512) hidden units.
A configuration for the LLFF dataset that adapts the Mip-NeRF framework.
It differs from the Blender configuration by keeping the distortion regularizer enabled and using Charbonnier loss instead of MSE.
On the LLFF dataset with 256 hidden units, Mip-NeRF achieves PSNR 26.93, SSIM 0.830, LPIPS 0.177, Time 2.48 hrs, Params 0.61M.
The variant "Our Model" achieves PSNR 26.68, SSIM 0.847, LPIPS 0.150, Time 2.39 hrs, Params 0.84M.
With 512 hidden units, Mip-NeRF achieves PSNR 27.01, SSIM 0.845, LPIPS 0.148, Time 6.15 hrs, Params 2.27M, while "Our Model" achieves PSNR 26.86, SSIM 0.858, LPIPS 0.128, Time 3.84 hrs, Params 3.23M.
A configuration for training Neural Unsigned Distance Fields.
It uses the ADAM optimizer with a learning rate that warms up to $2 \times 10^{-4}$ in the first 5k iterations and decreases to $1 \times 10^{-5}$ by the end.
The batch size is 512 random rays sampled from 8 randomly selected camera poses per iteration.
A configuration for NeRF-SDP, which uses a Res-UNet and other components.
It uses the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of $1 \times 10^{-3}$ for the Res-UNet and $5 \times 10^{-4}$ for other parts.
Training runs for 250,000 steps on an Nvidia GeForce RTX 3090.
The first 170,000 steps optimize auxiliary and rendering losses jointly, while the last 80,000 steps optimize only the rendering loss.
Feature dimensions are 24 for 2D features and 8 for 3D features.
A configuration for high-fidelity neural surface reconstruction using SDFs.
It samples pixels randomly without tracking statistics, using long training iterations (500k) to reduce stochasticity.
The ROI is assumed to be inside a unit sphere.
Inactive hash resolutions have feature vectors set to zero.
The learning rate is $1 \times 10^{-3}$ with a linear warmup of 5k iterations, decaying by a factor of 10 at 300k and 400k iterations.
It uses AdamW with weight decay $10^{-2}$ and $w_{iek} = 0.1$.
The SDF MLP has one layer, and the color MLP has four layers.
A configuration for generating objects in NeRFs.
The generation model is optimized on a single Nvidia 3090 GPU for 20,000 iterations, with 30% of iterations trained with background augmentation.
A configuration for Tri-MipRF, which uses a tri-mip representation.
The base mipmap shape $M_{l0}$ is $H=512, W=512, C=16$.
It uses the AdamW optimizer with weight decay $1 \times 10^{-5}$ and learning rate $2 \times 10^{-3}$, scheduled by MultiStepLR.
The learning rate for the Tri-Mip encoding is scaled up 10x relative to the MLP.
It uses an area loss $L_{area}$, scaling pixel loss by the footprint area.
A variant of nerfacto using a standard MLP density field instead of HashMLPDensityField.
For the Blender dataset, near/far thresholds are $t_n=2.0, t_f=6.0$.
Camera optimizer, appearance embedding, distortion loss, and scene contraction are disabled.
